column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|07-15|1946|Χασανάλ Μπολκιάχ|Hassanal Bolkiah|Hassanal Bolkiah has been Sultan of Brunei since 1967. He is also the prime minister and the minister of foreign affairs and finance of the country, and he is considered one of the richest leaders in the world thanks to oil and natural gas.

bio|07-15|2017|Μάρτιν Λαντάου|Martin Landau|Martin Landau was an American actor. He won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for playing Bela Lugosi in "Ed Wood" and also appeared in the series "Mission: Impossible". He died in 2017.

bio|07-16|1557|Άννα της Κλέβης|Anne of Cleves|Anne of Cleves was the fourth wife of Henry VIII of England. The marriage was annulled in 1540, a few months after it was contracted, and she lived in England with the title "the king's sister". She died in 1557.

bio|07-16|1764|Ιβάν ΣΤ΄|Ivan VI|Ivan VI became Tsar of Russia as an infant, in 1740, and was deposed after a year. He lived imprisoned and was killed in 1764 in an attempt to free himself, inside the fortress of Shlisselburg.

bio|07-16|1872|Ρόαλντ Αμούνδσεν|Roald Amundsen|Roald Amundsen was a Norwegian explorer. He led the team that first reached the South Pole, in December 1911, and he was the first to traverse the Northwest Passage. He was lost in 1928 on a rescue mission.

bio|07-16|1907|Μπάρμπαρα Στάνγουικ|Barbara Stanwyck|Barbara Stanwyck was an American actress. She played in films such as "Double Indemnity" by Billy Wilder and "Stella Dallas", and she had a long career in cinema and television. She died in 1990.

bio|07-16|1983|Κατρίνα Κεφ|Katrina Kaif|Katrina Kaif is a British actress of Indian origin who lives and works in Bollywood. She has starred in many commercially successful films and is one of the best-known actresses in the country.

bio|07-16|1985|Χάινριχ Μπελ|Heinrich Böll|Heinrich Böll was a German writer. He wrote about Germany during and after the war, with works such as "The Lost Honour of Katharina Blum". In 1972 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|07-16|1988|Σέρχιο Μπουσκέτς|Sergio Busquets|Sergio Busquets is a Spanish footballer who plays as a defensive midfielder. He played for Barcelona and Inter Miami and won the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 with Spain.

bio|07-16|1989|Γκάρεθ Μπέιλ|Gareth Bale|Gareth Bale is a former Welsh footballer. He played for Tottenham and Real Madrid, where he won five Champions Leagues. He is the top scorer in the history of Wales and led his national team to Euro 2016.

bio|07-16|1989|Χέρμπερτ φον Κάραγιαν|Herbert von Karajan|Herbert von Karajan was an Austrian conductor. He led the Berlin Philharmonic for thirty years, from 1955, and became one of the best-known and most recorded conductors of the 20th century.

bio|07-17|1588|Μιμάρ Σινάν|Mimar Sinan|Mimar Sinan was the great architect of the Ottomans. He was born a Christian in Cappadocia and worked under sultans such as Suleiman the Magnificent. He built hundreds of buildings, the most important being the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne.

bio|07-17|1790|Άνταμ Σμιθ|Adam Smith|Adam Smith was a Scottish philosopher and economist. His work "The Wealth of Nations", published in 1776, is considered fundamental to classical economics, and he proposed the idea of the market's "invisible hand".

bio|07-17|1888|Σαμουήλ Ιωσήφ Άγκνον|Shmuel Yosef Agnon|Shmuel Yosef Agnon was born in present-day Ukraine and wrote in Hebrew. He was one of the leading writers of Israel. In 1966 he shared the Nobel Prize in Literature with Nelly Sachs. He died in 1970.

bio|07-17|1899|Τζέιμς Κάγκνεϊ|James Cagney|James Cagney was an American actor. He became known as a gangster in the films of the 1930s, such as "The Public Enemy", and he won an Oscar for "Yankee Doodle Dandy", in which he also danced.

bio|07-17|1912|Ανρί Πουανκαρέ|Henri Poincaré|Henri Poincaré was a French mathematician, physicist and philosopher of science. He contributed to topology and to the theory of dynamical systems and formulated the well-known Poincaré conjecture, which was proved in 2003.

bio|07-17|1918|Νικόλαος Β΄|Nicholas II|Nicholas II was the last Tsar of Russia, from 1894. He abdicated in 1917 after the February Revolution. The Bolsheviks executed him, together with his family, in Yekaterinburg in July 1918.

bio|07-17|1935|Ντόναλντ Σάδερλαντ|Donald Sutherland|Donald Sutherland was a Canadian actor. He appeared in the films "The Dirty Dozen", "M*A*S*H" and "Don't Look Now", and later in the trilogy "The Hunger Games". He died in 2024.

bio|07-17|1954|Άνγκελα Μέρκελ|Angela Merkel|Angela Merkel was born in Hamburg and grew up in East Germany. She was a physicist and became Chancellor of Germany from 2005 to 2021, the first woman to hold the post. She led the country through the financial crisis and the refugee crisis.
bio|07-17|1955|Λι Κετσιάνγκ|Li Keqiang|Li Keqiang was a Chinese politician. He served as Premier of China from 2013 to 2023 and focused mainly on the economy. He died in 2023.

bio|07-18|1100|Γοδεφρείδος του Μπουιγιόν|Godfrey of Bouillon|Godfrey of Bouillon was a leader of the First Crusade. After the capture of Jerusalem in 1099 he became the first ruler of the city, with the title "protector of the Holy Places". He died in 1100.

bio|07-18|1610|Καραβάτζιο|Caravaggio|Caravaggio was an Italian Baroque painter. He became known for his dramatic paintings, with strong contrasts of light and shadow. He had a violent character and was hunted for murder. He died in 1610, at the age of 38.

bio|07-18|1721|Αντουάν Βαττώ|Antoine Watteau|Antoine Watteau was a French Rococo painter. He painted "fêtes galantes", with nobles in parks, and became known for works such as "The Embarkation for Cythera". He died young, at the age of 36.

bio|07-18|1811|Ουίλλιαμ Θάκερυ|William Makepeace Thackeray|William Makepeace Thackeray was a British writer, born in India. He wrote the satirical novel "Vanity Fair". He was a contemporary and rival of Dickens. He died in 1863.

bio|07-18|1817|Τζέιν Όστεν|Jane Austen|Jane Austen was an English writer. She wrote the novels "Pride and Prejudice", "Emma" and "Sense and Sensibility", with a humorous look at the society of her time. She died in 1817, at the age of 41.

bio|07-18|1853|Χέντρικ Λόρεντς|Hendrik Lorentz|Hendrik Lorentz was a Dutch physicist. He formulated the Lorentz transformations, which Einstein later used in special relativity. In 1902 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pieter Zeeman. He died in 1928.

bio|07-18|1918|Νέλσον Μαντέλα|Nelson Mandela|Nelson Mandela was a South African politician. He was imprisoned for 27 years for his struggle against apartheid, and after his release in 1990 he became, in 1994, the first Black president of South Africa. He died in 2013.

bio|07-18|1967|Βιν Ντίζελ|Vin Diesel|Vin Diesel is an American actor and producer. He became known for the "Fast and Furious" film series, in which he plays Dominic Toretto, and he is the voice of Groot in "Guardians of the Galaxy".

bio|07-18|1982|Πριγιάνκα Τσόπρα|Priyanka Chopra|Priyanka Chopra is an Indian actress, producer and singer. She won the Miss World title in 2000 and built a career in Bollywood and Hollywood, including the series "Quantico".

bio|07-19|1374|Πετράρχης|Petrarch|Petrarch was an Italian poet and scholar, one of the first humanists. He wrote the "Canzoniere", a collection of love sonnets for Laura. He died in 1374 at Arquà, near Padua.

bio|07-19|1543|Μαρία Μπολέυν|Mary Boleyn|Mary Boleyn was an English noblewoman and the sister of Anne Boleyn. She was a mistress of Henry VIII before her sister. Her life also became known through the novel "The Other Boleyn Girl". She died in 1543.

bio|07-19|1814|Σάμουελ Κολτ|Samuel Colt|Samuel Colt was an American inventor. In 1836 he patented the revolver with a rotating cylinder and founded the Colt company, which became one of the largest arms manufacturers.

bio|07-19|1834|Εντγκάρ Ντεγκά|Edgar Degas|Edgar Degas was a French painter and sculptor, associated with Impressionism. He was known for scenes of dancers and horse races and for his dynamic compositions. He died in 1917.

bio|07-19|1893|Βλαντίμιρ Μαγιακόφσκι|Vladimir Mayakovsky|Vladimir Mayakovsky was a Russian poet of Futurism and a supporter of the October Revolution. He wrote poetry and plays in a pioneering style. He committed suicide in 1930.

bio|07-19|1947|Μπράιαν Μέι|Brian May|Brian May is an English guitarist and astrophysicist. He was the guitarist of Queen and composed songs such as "We Will Rock You". He holds a doctorate in astrophysics.

bio|07-19|1976|Μπένεντικτ Κάμπερμπατς|Benedict Cumberbatch|Benedict Cumberbatch is an English actor. He became known as Sherlock Holmes in the BBC series "Sherlock" and played in the films "Doctor Strange" and "The Imitation Game".

bio|07-19|2014|Τζέιμς Γκάρνερ|James Garner|James Garner was an American actor. He became known for the series "Maverick" and "The Rockford Files" and for films such as "The Great Escape". He died in 2014.

bio|07-19|2016|Γκάρυ Μάρσαλ|Garry Marshall|Garry Marshall was an American director and producer. He directed the films "Pretty Woman" and "Runaway Bride" and created television series such as "Happy Days". He died in 2016.

bio|07-20|1304|Πετράρχης|Petrarch|Petrarch was born in 1304 in Arezzo, Tuscany. He was a poet and scholar and is considered one of the first humanists. He wrote the "Canzoniere", with his love sonnets for Laura.

bio|07-20|1822|Γκρέγκορ Μέντελ|Gregor Mendel|Gregor Mendel was an Austrian monk and botanist. Through experiments on peas he discovered the basic laws of heredity and is regarded as the father of genetics. His work was recognised after his death, in 1884.

bio|07-20|1864|Έρικ Άξελ Κάρλφελντ|Erik Axel Karlfeldt|Erik Axel Karlfeldt was a Swedish poet. In 1931 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature posthumously. He had declined the prize in 1918, while he was secretary of the Swedish Academy.

bio|07-20|1866|Μπέρναρντ Ρίμαν|Bernhard Riemann|Bernhard Riemann was a German mathematician. He contributed to differential geometry, complex analysis and number theory, with the famous Riemann hypothesis. Later, Einstein used his work. He died young, at the age of 39.

bio|07-20|1919|Έντμουντ Χίλαρι|Edmund Hillary|Edmund Hillary was a New Zealand mountaineer. In 1953, together with the Sherpa Tenzing Norgay, he became the first to reach the summit of Everest. He died in 2008.

bio|07-20|1937|Γουλιέλμο Μαρκόνι|Guglielmo Marconi|Guglielmo Marconi was an Italian inventor. He developed wireless telegraphy and in 1901 sent a radio signal across the Atlantic. In 1909 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Karl Ferdinand Braun.

bio|07-20|1966|Ενρίκε Πένια Νιέτο|Enrique Peña Nieto|Enrique Peña Nieto is a Mexican politician. He was president of Mexico from 2012 to 2018. His term was marked by reforms but also by corruption scandals.

bio|07-20|1973|Μπρους Λι|Bruce Lee|Bruce Lee was born in San Francisco and grew up in Hong Kong. He was an actor and a pioneer of the martial arts, with films such as "Enter the Dragon". He died suddenly in 1973, at the age of 32.
bio|07-20|2017|Τσέστερ Μπένινγκτον|Chester Bennington|Chester Bennington was the singer of the American band Linkin Park, with hits such as "In the End" and "Numb". He died in 2017, at the age of 41.

bio|07-21|1796|Ρόμπερτ Μπερνς|Robert Burns|Robert Burns was a Scottish poet and is regarded as the national poet of Scotland. He wrote in the Scots dialect, and the song "Auld Lang Syne" is sung on New Year's Eve. He died in 1796.

bio|07-21|1899|Έρνεστ Χέμινγουεϊ|Ernest Hemingway|Ernest Hemingway was born in 1899 in Illinois. He was an American writer with a spare style. He wrote "The Old Man and the Sea" and in 1954 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1961.
bio|07-21|1944|Τζον Άτα Μιλς|John Atta Mills|John Atta Mills was a Ghanaian politician. He was president of Ghana from 2009 to 2012, when he died in office.

bio|07-21|1944|Κλάους φον Στάουφενμπεργκ|Claus von Stauffenberg|Claus von Stauffenberg was a German officer. He led the failed assassination attempt on Hitler on 20 July 1944. He was executed that night, a few hours later.

bio|07-21|1951|Ρόμπιν Ουίλιαμς|Robin Williams|Robin Williams was an American actor and comedian, known for his improvisation. He played in the films "Good Morning, Vietnam", "Dead Poets Society" and "Good Will Hunting", for which he won an Oscar. He died in 2014.

bio|07-21|1967|Άλμπερτ Λουτούλι|Albert Lutuli|Albert Lutuli was a South African politician. He was president of the African National Congress and in 1960 was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, as the first African to receive it. He died in 1967.

bio|07-21|1971|Σαρλότ Γκανσμπούρ|Charlotte Gainsbourg|Charlotte Gainsbourg is a French-British actress and singer. She is the daughter of Serge Gainsbourg and Jane Birkin and has played in films such as "Melancholia" by Lars von Trier.

bio|07-21|1978|Τζος Χάρτνετ|Josh Hartnett|Josh Hartnett is an American actor. He played in the films "Pearl Harbor", "Black Hawk Down" and "Helen of Troy". He became known through the television series "Lost".

bio|07-22|1461|Κάρολος Ζ΄|Charles VII|Charles VII was King of France from 1422 to 1461. With the help of Joan of Arc he defeated the English in the Hundred Years' War and recovered France. He died in 1461.

bio|07-22|1784|Φρίντριχ Μπέσελ|Friedrich Bessel|Friedrich Bessel was a German astronomer and mathematician. In 1838 he measured for the first time the distance to a star, 61 Cygni, using the method of parallax. Bessel functions bear his name.
bio|07-22|1826|Τζιουζέπε Πιάτσι|Giuseppe Piazzi|Giuseppe Piazzi was an Italian astronomer and monk. In 1801 he discovered Ceres, the first asteroid. He died in 1826 in Palermo.

bio|07-22|1878|Γιάνους Κόρτσακ|Janusz Korczak|Janusz Korczak was a Polish-Jewish pediatrician and educator. He ran an orphanage in Warsaw and stayed with his children when they were taken to the Treblinka camp, where they were murdered in 1942.

bio|07-22|1887|Γκούσταβ Χερτς|Gustav Hertz|Gustav Hertz was a German physicist and the nephew of Heinrich Hertz. In 1925 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with James Franck, for experiments on collisions between electrons and atoms.

bio|07-22|1955|Γουίλεμ Νταφόε|Willem Dafoe|Willem Dafoe is an American actor. He became known for his roles in the films "Platoon" and "Spider-Man", where he played the Green Goblin, and in "The Lighthouse". He has been nominated for the Oscar several times.

bio|07-22|1967|Καρλ Σάντμπεργκ|Carl Sandburg|Carl Sandburg was an American poet and biographer. He wrote poetry about ordinary people and about Chicago and was awarded Pulitzer Prizes, for his poetry and for his biography of Lincoln. He died in 1967.

bio|07-22|1992|Σελίνα Γκόμεζ|Selena Gomez|Selena Gomez is an American singer and actress. She became known through the children's series "Wizards of Waverly Place" and starred in the series "Only Murders in the Building". She also has her own cosmetics company.

bio|07-22|2025|Όζι Όζμπορν|Ozzy Osbourne|Ozzy Osbourne was an English singer, founder of Black Sabbath and a pioneer of heavy metal. He was known as "the Prince of Darkness". He died on 22 July 2025, a few weeks after his last concert.

bio|07-23|1885|Οδυσσεύς Γκραντ|Ulysses S. Grant|Ulysses S. Grant was a general and the 18th president of the United States. He led the Union army to victory in the American Civil War and was president from 1869 to 1877. He died in 1885.

bio|07-23|1892|Χαϊλέ Σελασιέ Α΄|Haile Selassie I|Haile Selassie I was Emperor of Ethiopia from 1930 to 1974. He symbolised the resistance to the Italian invasion of 1935 and was an important figure for the Rastafari movement. He was deposed by a military coup.

bio|07-23|1916|Ουίλιαμ Ράμσεϊ|William Ramsay|William Ramsay was a Scottish chemist. He discovered the noble gases, such as argon, neon, krypton and xenon, and in 1904 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|07-23|1941|Σέρτζιο Ματαρέλα|Sergio Mattarella|Sergio Mattarella is an Italian lawyer and politician. He has been President of the Italian Republic since 2015 and was re-elected in 2022. Previously he was also a judge of the Constitutional Court.

bio|07-23|1951|Φιλίπ Πεταίν|Philippe Pétain|Philippe Pétain was a French marshal and a hero of the Battle of Verdun in the First World War. In 1940 he led the collaborationist Vichy government, and after the war he was convicted of treason. He died in prison in 1951.

bio|07-23|1967|Φίλιπ Σέιμουρ Χόφμαν|Philip Seymour Hoffman|Philip Seymour Hoffman was an American actor and director. He won an Oscar for his performance in "Capote". He also played in "Magnolia" and "Doubt". He died in 2014.

bio|07-23|1989|Ντάνιελ Ράντκλιφ|Daniel Radcliffe|Daniel Radcliffe is an English actor. He became known worldwide as Harry Potter in the film series of the same name and later played various roles in cinema and theatre.

bio|07-23|2011|Έιμι Γουάινχαουζ|Amy Winehouse|Amy Winehouse was an English jazz and soul singer. She became known with the album "Back to Black" and the song "Rehab". She died in 2011, at the age of 27.

bio|07-24|1783|Σιμόν Μπολίβαρ|Simón Bolívar|Simón Bolívar was born in Caracas. He led the struggle for independence from Spain in several South American countries, and he was called "the Liberator". Bolivia bears his name. He died in 1830.

bio|07-24|1862|Μάρτιν Βαν Μπιούρεν|Martin Van Buren|Martin Van Buren was the 8th president of the United States, from 1837 to 1841. His term was marked by an economic crisis. Before that he was vice president under Andrew Jackson. He died in 1862.

bio|07-24|1895|Ρόμπερτ Γκρέιβς|Robert Graves|Robert Graves was an English poet and writer. He wrote the autobiographical "Goodbye to All That" and the historical novel "I, Claudius". He also engaged with Greek myths. He died in 1985.

bio|07-24|1897|Αμέλια Έρχαρτ|Amelia Earhart|Amelia Earhart was an American pilot and writer. In 1932 she became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic. She disappeared in 1937 while attempting to fly around the world.

bio|07-24|1927|Ρυουνοσούκε Ακουταγκάβα|Ryūnosuke Akutagawa|Ryūnosuke Akutagawa was a Japanese writer, a master of the short story. He wrote "Rashomon" and "In a Grove", which inspired Kurosawa's film. He committed suicide in 1927, at the age of 35.

bio|07-24|1957|Σαβκάτ Μιρζιγιάγιεφ|Shavkat Mirziyoyev|Shavkat Mirziyoyev is an Uzbek politician. He was prime minister and since 2016 has been president of Uzbekistan, where he has gradually opened the country to the outside world.

bio|07-24|1969|Τζένιφερ Λόπεζ|Jennifer Lopez|Jennifer Lopez is an American singer, actress and businesswoman. She became known with the films "Selena" and "Maid in Manhattan" and with hits such as "Jenny from the Block".

bio|07-24|1974|Τζέιμς Τσάντγουικ|James Chadwick|James Chadwick was an English physicist. In 1932 he discovered the neutron and in 1935 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He also took part in the atomic bomb programme.

bio|07-24|1991|Ισαάκ Μπάσεβις Σίνγκερ|Isaac Bashevis Singer|Isaac Bashevis Singer was a Polish-Jewish writer who wrote in Yiddish and lived in the United States. He wrote short stories about the Jewish world of Poland and in 1978 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|07-25|306|Κωνστάντιος Α΄ Χλωρός|Constantius I Chlorus|Constantius I Chlorus was a Roman emperor and the father of Constantine the Great. He was Caesar and then Augustus in the Tetrarchy. He died in 306 at Eboracum, present-day York, and the soldiers proclaimed his son emperor.

bio|07-25|1471|Θωμάς ο Κεμπήσιος|Thomas à Kempis|Thomas à Kempis was a German priest and monk. He is credited with the book "The Imitation of Christ", one of the most widely read Christian works of spirituality. He died in 1471.

bio|07-25|1564|Φερδινάνδος Α΄|Ferdinand I|Ferdinand I was Holy Roman Emperor from 1558 to 1564. The brother of Charles V, he was also king of Hungary and Bohemia, and he tried to halt the Ottomans in Europe.

bio|07-25|1894|Γκαβρίλο Πρίντσιπ|Gavrilo Princip|Gavrilo Princip was a Bosnian Serb nationalist. In 1914 in Sarajevo he assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand, an event that led to the First World War. He died in prison in 1918.

bio|07-25|1905|Ελίας Κανέττι|Elias Canetti|Elias Canetti was born in Bulgaria into a Sephardic family and wrote in German. He wrote the novel "Auto-da-Fé" and the essay "Crowds and Power". In 1981 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|07-25|1920|Ρόζαλιντ Φράνκλιν|Rosalind Franklin|Rosalind Franklin was an English chemist and crystallographer. The X-ray diffraction images she took of DNA were critical to the discovery of the double helix. She died in 1958, at the age of 37.
bio|07-25|1967|Ματ ΛεΜπλάνκ|Matt LeBlanc|Matt LeBlanc is an American actor. He became known as Joey Tribbiani in the series "Friends" and in its spin-off "Joey".

bio|07-25|1978|Λουίζ Μπράουν|Louise Brown|Louise Brown was born in England and was the first child born through in vitro fertilisation. The doctors Patrick Steptoe and Robert Edwards helped with her birth.

bio|07-25|1980|Βλαντίμιρ Βισότσκι Ρώσος τραγουδιστής|Vladimir Vysotsky|Vladimir Vysotsky was a Russian singer-songwriter and actor. His songs, with guitar and lyrics about everyday life, were very popular in the Soviet Union. He died in 1980, at the age of 42.

bio|07-26|1856|Τζορτζ Μπέρναρντ Σω|George Bernard Shaw|George Bernard Shaw was born in Dublin and was a playwright. He wrote "Pygmalion", which inspired the musical "My Fair Lady". In 1925 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|07-26|1867|Όθων Α΄|Otto|Otto was the first King of Greece, from 1833 until 1862, when he was overthrown. He was born in Bavaria. In 1843 he was forced to grant a constitution. He died in Bamberg in 1867.

bio|07-26|1875|Καρλ Γκούσταβ Γιουνγκ|Carl Gustav Jung|Carl Gustav Jung was a Swiss psychiatrist. He founded analytical psychology and introduced concepts such as the collective unconscious and archetypes. He was initially a collaborator of Freud. He died in 1961.
bio|07-26|1894|Άλντους Χάξλεϋ|Aldous Huxley|Aldous Huxley was an English writer. He wrote the dystopian novel "Brave New World" in 1932 and "The Doors of Perception". He died in 1963.

bio|07-26|1925|Γκότλομπ Φρέγκε|Gottlob Frege|Gottlob Frege was a German mathematician, logician and philosopher. He is considered the founder of modern mathematical logic and analytic philosophy. A letter from Bertrand Russell revealed a contradiction in his system.

bio|07-26|1928|Στάνλεϊ Κούμπρικ|Stanley Kubrick|Stanley Kubrick was an American director. He directed the films "2001: A Space Odyssey", "A Clockwork Orange" and "The Shining", known for his perfectionism. He died in 1999.
bio|07-26|1952|Εβίτα Περόν|Eva Perón|Eva Perón, known as Evita, was the wife of Argentine president Juan Perón and was greatly loved by the poor. She died of cancer in 1952, at the age of 33.

bio|07-26|1964|Σάντρα Μπούλοκ|Sandra Bullock|Sandra Bullock is an American actress. She became known with the film "Speed" and won the Oscar for Best Actress for "The Blind Side". She also appeared in "Gravity".

bio|07-27|1612|Μουράτ Δ΄|Murad IV|Murad IV was an Ottoman sultan from 1623 to 1640. He came to the throne as a child and later imposed strict authority. He retook Baghdad from the Persians in 1638. He died young, at the age of 27.

bio|07-27|1824|Αλέξανδρος Δουμάς (υιός)|Alexandre Dumas fils|Alexandre Dumas fils was a French writer and the son of the author of "The Three Musketeers". He wrote the novel and play "La Dame aux Camélias", which inspired the opera "La Traviata". He died in 1895.

bio|07-27|1835|Τζοζουέ Καρντούτσι|Giosuè Carducci|Giosuè Carducci was an Italian poet and professor of literature. In 1906 he became the first Italian to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1907.

bio|07-27|1841|Μιχαήλ Λέρμοντοφ|Mikhail Lermontov|Mikhail Lermontov was a Russian poet and writer of Romanticism. He wrote the novel "A Hero of Our Time". He was killed in a duel in 1841, at the age of 26.

bio|07-27|1844|Τζων Ντάλτον|John Dalton|John Dalton was an English chemist and physicist. He formulated the atomic theory of matter and described the law of partial pressures of gases. He also studied his own colour blindness, which was named "Daltonism".

bio|07-27|1969|Triple H|Triple H|Triple H, whose real name is Paul Levesque, is an American wrestler and WWE executive. He became known as a champion in professional wrestling and later took up an executive position in the company.

bio|07-27|1980|Μοχάμεντ Ρεζά Παχλαβί|Mohammad Reza Pahlavi|Mohammad Reza Pahlavi was the last Shah of Iran, from 1941 to 1979. He was overthrown by the Islamic Revolution and went into exile. He died in Cairo in 1980.

bio|07-27|1987|Μάρεκ Χάμσικ|Marek Hamšík|Marek Hamšík is a former Slovak footballer. He played as a midfielder for Napoli and was captain of the Slovakia national team, in which he has played the most matches.

bio|07-27|2015|Αμπντούλ Καλάμ|A. P. J. Abdul Kalam|Abdul Kalam was an Indian scientist and politician. He developed missiles and was the 11th president of India, from 2002 to 2007, also known as "the People's President". He died in 2015.

bio|07-28|1741|Αντόνιο Βιβάλντι|Antonio Vivaldi|Antonio Vivaldi was an Italian Baroque composer and violinist from Venice. He wrote more than five hundred concertos, the best known being "The Four Seasons". He died in Vienna in 1741.
